body: May overlooked upside dito: hindi kailangang pure vendor lock-in ang cross-company co-simulation. The Modelica Association's DCP is an open, fee-free standard for connecting models/real-time systems across vendors, while Toshiba says VenetDCP supports FMI and many major simulators. So ang mas interesting test sa summit is not just 'gumagana ba ang Toshiba demo?' but whether companies can preserve model IP while keeping interfaces portable enough to avoid one-vendor dependence.

claims.text: DCP is a Modelica Association standard whose specification and related files are available under open-source licenses without a usage fee.
Toshiba says VenetDCP supports FMI and a broad set of engineering simulators while allowing distributed co-simulation without handing over the complete confidential model.
Open interface standards can reduce some switching-cost and interoperability risk, although actual portability still depends on implementation quality and model semantics.
claims.basis: Inference from standards availability and supported-tool claims
